title: 2026-11-04_XMRig_Cryptominer_Investigation_9f3
description: Investigate systems for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining software and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The IT department has received reports of unusually high CPU usage on several Linux servers in the network. Initial investigations suggest that one of the servers might be running unauthorized cryptocurrency mining software. Your task is to investigate these systems, identify the source of the problem, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the `miner-host` system with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the `miner-host` system:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the `miner-host` system to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the `miner-host` system using the provided credentials.
2. List all running services using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service`
3. Look for any suspicious or unauthorized services. Pay attention to services with unusual names or those that you don't recognize.
4. Investigate the suspicious service by checking its status, configuration, and executable path.
5. The final flag is `sys-monitor.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status and details of a specific service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the executable path of the service to see if it points to a suspicious location.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to system monitoring or hardware performance, as these could be disguising malicious activity.

levels.title: Identify High Resource Usage Process
levels.content: Identify the process responsible for the abnormal CPU or resource utilization on the `miner-host` system.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the `miner-host` system using the provided credentials.
2. Check the running processes and their resource usage with the command: `top`
3. Look for any processes consuming a high percentage of CPU resources.
4. Investigate the suspicious process by checking its name, path, and user.
5. Use the command `ps aux | grep <process_name>` to gather more information about the process.
6. The final flag is `sys-monitor`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Pay attention to processes with high CPU usage percentages.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the process name and path to see if they look suspicious or unusual.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for processes that might be related to system monitoring or hardware performance, as these could be disguising malicious activity.

levels.title: Determine External Communication
levels.content: Determine the external host communicating with the compromised `miner-host` system for cryptocurrency mining.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the `miner-host` system using the provided credentials.
2. Check the network connections using the command: `netstat -tulnp`
3. Look for any suspicious outbound connections, especially those to external hosts.
4. Investigate the suspicious connection by checking the destination IP address and port.
5. Use the command `curl -v <destination_IP>:<port>` to gather more information about the connection.
6. The final flag is `192.168.40.5`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Pay attention to outbound connections to external hosts, especially those on unusual ports.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the destination IP address and port to see if they match known mining pool or command-and-control servers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for connections that might be related to system monitoring or hardware performance, as these could be disguising malicious activity.
